_comment: Conversations, not sentences. Each is several turns from one person, and each turn is scored with every earlier turn and every earlier answer in front of the model, the way a host keeps them. They are written in the patterns older adults were recorded using with voice assistants at home, not in the phrasing a tool description suggests: a month of recorded Alexa use where a quarter of turns failed and repeating, rephrasing, 'never mind', 'thank you' and 'I got it' were how people repaired or ended (Mahmood, Wang and Huang, arXiv 2403.02421); and 844 recorded medication check-ins whose breakdowns were mostly about earlier turns ('What about yesterday though?'), asking why ('why are you asking me now?') and stepping off the script ('let me go check with my wife') (Mathur and others, arXiv 2510.06690). The heat details follow what firefighters and health officers describe: older people in hot homes whose cooling is not working (KFF Health News). tool null means the right answer calls nothing. anyOf lists the tools that are each a reasonable reading.

conversations.name: a dangerous day, carried through
conversations.pattern: one request leading to the next

turns.say: Alexa, is it safe for me to go out today
ok when then
I have to get to the pharmacy anyway
thank you, that's all

conversations.name: the same thing twice, then never mind
conversations.pattern: repeating was the commonest repair, and 'never mind' ended many

turns.say: is it too hot for my pills today
is it too hot for my pills today
never mind

conversations.name: what about tomorrow though
conversations.pattern: 'What about yesterday though?': a follow-up that only means something after the answer before it

turns.say: when's a good time to water the garden
what about tomorrow though

conversations.name: asking why
conversations.pattern: 'why are you asking me now?': explanations were a third of breakdowns

turns.say: can I sit out on the porch
why, I feel fine

conversations.name: feeling unwell partway through
conversations.pattern: a symptom said in passing, then asking for family

turns.say: I'm going to walk to the mailbox, is that ok
ummm actually I feel a bit dizzy
tell my daughter

conversations.name: the air conditioner gives out
conversations.pattern: older homes whose cooling is not working

turns.say: my air conditioner just stopped working
it's eighty six in here
where can I go then
let my son know I'm going to the library

conversations.name: a storm, then the power
conversations.pattern: a worry, then the thing happening

turns.say: there's a storm warning, what do I do about my insulin
the power just went out, where can I go

conversations.name: a new medicine
conversations.pattern: telling it in passing, then asking what it changes

turns.say: the doctor started me on Lasix
does that change anything about today

conversations.name: the wrong wake word and a pause

turns.say: Alexis, um, how bad is the heat for me
and later on
I want to do some gardening for an hour, when
no, two hours

conversations.name: off the script, then back
conversations.pattern: 'Is the extreme heat natural to weather?', then a question it can answer

turns.say: is all this heat natural
ok, when can I walk the dog
I just got back from the shops, I felt fine
actually I was a bit lightheaded on the way back

conversations.name: a daughter checks in
conversations.pattern: a caregiver asking about somebody else

turns.say: how is Mum doing today
should I go round this afternoon

conversations.name: the cold, and getting home
conversations.pattern: a symptom, then the end of it

turns.say: my hands are numb and I'm shivering
I'm inside now, I got it, thanks
turns._why: Ending the conversation is right, and so is recording the outing that left their hands numb.
